Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The same Firewall build, geared against its own worst property instead of around it. The base build's guide is blunt about the flaw: 'the moment you leave the Ring of Fire you suddenly deal no damage', which is why Maxroll's week-1 read calls Firewall the strongest single-target damage in the game and slow and clunky to play in the same sentence. The base build then makes that worse at the push stage, where swapping Berú of the Threefold for Berú of the Cauldron plus Aspect of Ancient Flame turns cooldown reduction into a stat that actively reduces Firewall damage, capping it at four or five rolls. This variant refuses that swap. It keeps Berú of the Threefold end to end, keeps stacking cooldown reduction, and spends it on Teleport and Ice Armor uptime so that re-establishing a Ring of Fire is fast rather than something you commit to. The cost is real and worth stating: less peak damage per Ring, and a lower Pit ceiling than the base build's push variant. What you get back is a character that can move.

Rotation
  1. Unstable Currents and Ice Armor up, then hold the stagger - Charged Bolts for the Shock proc, Teleport into a body for the second, Hydra for the Cold proc - on a roughly two-second cadence so a Ring of Fire is always underfoot.
  2. Play that cadence while moving between two or three Rings rather than defending one.
Variants

Leveling — Unchanged from the base build at this stage: Firewall under the pack, Inferno to pull, Hydra for uptime, Teleport out. The difference is a habit rather than a rotation - get used to Teleporting the moment the Ring is no longer under anything, rather than finishing the cast.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and Vision of the Firestorm in hand.

Early Endgame — Berú of the Threefold auto-casts Meteor, Blizzard and Ball Lightning; the real skill is staggering the Frost and Pyromancy procs onto a roughly two-second cadence so a Ring of Fire is always underfoot. The Shock proc fires every six seconds and cannot be steered. This variant plays that cadence while moving between two or three Rings rather than defending one.
Move on when Raiment of the Infinite and Drognan's Anguish equipped, and your cooldown reduction is high enough that Teleport is available between packs rather than between rooms.

Late Endgame — Same cadence. The tell that this variant is working is that you are never standing still waiting for a cooldown; if you are, the base build's push variant is simply the better character and you should play that instead.
Move on when Paragon boards fully attached with their glyphs at 100, and you are choosing between this page and the base build's push variant. Choose this one only if you actually want to move.

Pushing — Untested at the very top of the Pit, and honest about why: the base build's push variant gives up mobility precisely because that is where the last few tiers come from. This variant will clear faster and die less; it will not out-push the thing it is a variant of. If your goal is a Pit rank, play sorcerer-meta-firewall.

Lootfilter

Firewall Sorcerer - Maxroll Light / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

The base build's own three in-guide import codes, and they fit this variant unchanged because the affix pool is identical - damage over time, Vulnerable, Intelligence, cooldown reduction. Prefer the Medium tier: this variant wants more cooldown reduction rolls than the base build, so a Strict endgame filter tuned to the push variant will hide jewelry you actually want.

Uniques
  • helm Sorcerer class unique. Dedicated table: Grigoire, The Galvanic Saint, in the Hall of the Penitent south of Ked Bardu, Dry Steppes; 1x Lair Key, key from Helltide. Where →
  • chest Sorcerer class unique. Dedicated table: Bartuc, reached through Infernal Hordes in Kehjistan near the Yshari Sanctum waypoint; 1x Infernal Hordes Compass, gather 666 Burning Aether. Where →
  • ring 2 Sorcerer class unique. Dedicated table: Andariel, in Hanged Man's Hall east of Tarsarak, Kehjistan; 1x Greater Lair Key, keys from the Initiate lair bosses. Where →
  • pants All-class unique. General Unique Pool from any lair boss, and gambling pants at the vendor is the cheap parallel route. Where →

How to run them

Identical across all five of the guide's variants: hire Subo 'for maphack and Molotov Scorched Earth spam', reinforce with Raheir 'with Bastion on Injured for safety'. The Molotov pick is coherent rather than incidental - more Burning application on top of a Firewall DoT engine - and the maphack directly answers the build's own named weakness, that it cannot go fast. Icy Veins hires Varyana instead but agrees on Raheir and Bastion; its Sorcerer page is dated Season 9 / patch 2.3.0 and describes a completely different Firewall build, so that divergence is staleness rather than a live disagreement and Maxroll's Subo is what this build records.

Plan

Stated plainly, because the honest answer is unusual here: this guide publishes War Plans *widgets* but no War Plans prose. The only text under the section, repeated identically for all five variants, is 'selected nodes are what I consider mandatory, the rest is up to personal preference'. The picks below are therefore decoded from the guide's own planner payload rather than quoted from the article, and the payload allocates five of the seven activity trees - it touches Nightmare Dungeons, Helltide, Kurast Undercity, Lair Bosses and The Pit, and leaves Tree of Whispers and Infernal Hordes empty. That is the author's own board, so it is real build-specific data; it simply arrives without an explanation, and no explanation has been invented for it.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.
Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The same Firewall build, geared against its own worst property instead of around it. The base build's guide is blunt about the flaw: 'the moment you leave the Ring of Fire you suddenly deal no damage', which is why Maxroll's week-1 read calls Firewall the strongest single-target damage in the game and slow and clunky to play in the same sentence. The base build then makes that worse at the push stage, where swapping Berú of the Threefold for Berú of the Cauldron plus Aspect of Ancient Flame turns cooldown reduction into a stat that actively reduces Firewall damage, capping it at four or five rolls. This variant refuses that swap. It keeps Berú of the Threefold end to end, keeps stacking cooldown reduction, and spends it on Teleport and Ice Armor uptime so that re-establishing a Ring of Fire is fast rather than something you commit to. The cost is real and worth stating: less peak damage per Ring, and a lower Pit ceiling than the base build's push variant. What you get back is a character that can move.

Rotation
  1. Unstable Currents and Ice Armor up, then hold the stagger - Charged Bolts for the Shock proc, Teleport into a body for the second, Hydra for the Cold proc - on a roughly two-second cadence so a Ring of Fire is always underfoot.
  2. Play that cadence while moving between two or three Rings rather than defending one.
Variants

Leveling — Unchanged from the base build at this stage: Firewall under the pack, Inferno to pull, Hydra for uptime, Teleport out. The difference is a habit rather than a rotation - get used to Teleporting the moment the Ring is no longer under anything, rather than finishing the cast.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and Vision of the Firestorm in hand.

Early Endgame — Berú of the Threefold auto-casts Meteor, Blizzard and Ball Lightning; the real skill is staggering the Frost and Pyromancy procs onto a roughly two-second cadence so a Ring of Fire is always underfoot. The Shock proc fires every six seconds and cannot be steered. This variant plays that cadence while moving between two or three Rings rather than defending one.
Move on when Raiment of the Infinite and Drognan's Anguish equipped, and your cooldown reduction is high enough that Teleport is available between packs rather than between rooms.

Late Endgame — Same cadence. The tell that this variant is working is that you are never standing still waiting for a cooldown; if you are, the base build's push variant is simply the better character and you should play that instead.
Move on when Paragon boards fully attached with their glyphs at 100, and you are choosing between this page and the base build's push variant. Choose this one only if you actually want to move.

Pushing — Untested at the very top of the Pit, and honest about why: the base build's push variant gives up mobility precisely because that is where the last few tiers come from. This variant will clear faster and die less; it will not out-push the thing it is a variant of. If your goal is a Pit rank, play sorcerer-meta-firewall.

Reasoning

Based onRing of Fire Firewall Sorcerer
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. The push variant's Berú of the Cauldron plus Aspect of Ancient Flame package is never taken. The base guide's own consequence of taking it is that cooldown reduction 'directly reduces Firewall damage', capping the build at 4-5 cooldown rolls including tempers; this variant wants the opposite and keeps the endgame build's 1-2 extra rolls beyond helm and jewellery tempers.
  2. Aspect of the Untarnished Blaze and Conceited Aspect stay on the push gear where the base build swaps in Aspect of Ancient Flame and Aspect of Elemental Attunement - the same reasoning, applied to the aspect list rather than the charm set.
  3. Hydra stays on the push bar instead of the base build's Blizzard. Both are Berú of the Threefold proc feeders; Hydra keeps ticking while you reposition and Blizzard rewards standing still, which is exactly the axis this variant is trading on.
  4. Cooldown reduction leads the helm priority at every stage, including the push stage where the base build drops it for Maximum Life and Armor.
  5. The enchantment rule is unchanged and worth repeating because it is counter-intuitive: any orange enchantment will do, for the Fire damage from Enchantment Master, and the Firewall Enchantment is explicitly rejected - Burning has poor Lucky Hit Chance so it rarely procs and lands off to the side when it does.
  6. War Plans are inherited from the base build's planner payload unchanged; only the summary is re-worded, because a mobile cut of the build farms the same activities.

Chain Lightning gains 1 additional chains.

Blaze

UpgradeTeleport

Rank 1/3

Teleport becomes a Pyromancy Skill that deals 59.5% Fire damage.

Teleport now only dashes you forward a short distance and will consume 1 stack of Overpower to refund its Cooldown.

Ferocity

UpgradeTeleport

Rank 1/3

Teleport grants 2 stack of Ferocity if it hits an enemy.

Movement Speed

UpgradeTeleport

Rank 1/3

Teleport increases your Movement Speed by 10%[+] for 4 seconds.

Permafrost

UpgradeIce Armor

Rank 1/3

Ice Armor grants Unstoppable for 1 second and increases your Armor by 50% while active.

Cooldown Reduction

UpgradeIce Armor

Rank 1/3

Ice Armor's Cooldown is reduced to 16 seconds.

Duration Bonus and Barrier

UpgradeIce Armor

Rank 1/3

Ice Armor's duration is increased to 5 seconds and its Barrier amount is increased by 20%[x].

Cooldown Reduction

UpgradeHydra

Rank 1/3

Hydra reduces the Cooldown of a random Skill by 0.3 seconds whenever it attacks.

Healing

UpgradeHydra

Rank 1/3

Hydra heals you for 1% of your Maximum Life ({x}) each time it deals damage.

Behemoth

UpgradeHydra

Rank 1/3

Hydra Summons a massive 1-headed Hydra that spits explosive fire and deals 20% increased damage for each extra head it would have had.

Hydra no longer costs Mana, but has a 15 second Cooldown. You can now have up to 10 total Hydras at one time.

Duration Bonus

UpgradeLightning Spear

Rank 1/3

When a Lightning Spear Critically Strikes, its duration is increased by 0.1 seconds.

Reverse Polarity

UpgradeLightning Spear

Rank 1/3

Lightning Spear fires 2 spears that deal 96% damage Stun enemies for 1.0 second. Enemies can only be Stunned this way once every 5 seconds.

Critical Strike

UpgradeLightning Spear

Rank 1/3

Lightning Spear gains 10% increased Critical Strike Chance.

Hailstorm

UpgradeBlizzard

Rank 1/3

Blizzard forms Ice Spikes that explode twice if they hit a Vulnerable enemy, dealing 49% damage.

Seek and Duration Bonus

UpgradeBlizzard

Rank 1/3

Blizzard now seeks enemies and its duration is increased by 50%.

Barrier

UpgradeBlizzard

Rank 1/3

Blizzard grants you a Barrier that absorbs 0.5% of your Maximum Life for 4 seconds every second for each affected enemy.

Overpower

UpgradeMeteor

Rank 1/3

Meteor's Impact damage now grants 1 stack of Overpower per enemy hit.

Immobilize

UpgradeMeteor

Rank 1/3

Meteor Immobilizes enemies for 3 seconds on impact.

Air Burst

UpgradeMeteor

Rank 1/3

Meteor rains down 6 Meteorites before the final impact that each deal 45% damage each, but Meteor no longer deals Burning damage.

Ring of Fire

UpgradeFirewall

Rank 1/3

Firewall creates a ring of fire that deals 300% Fire damage over 3.5 seconds, but it now has a 12 second Cooldown.

Standing in this ring causes your Direct Damage to inflict this Burning damage to enemies.

Weaken

UpgradeFirewall

Rank 1/3

Firewall Weakens enemies for 2 seconds.

Crackling Energy

UpgradeBall Lightning

Rank 1/3

Ball Lightning forms 3 Crackling Energy when it dissipates.

Orbital

UpgradeBall Lightning

Rank 1/3

Ball Lightning orbits you and now deals 130 – 173% damage around you per second.

Cooldown Reduction

UpgradeUnstable Currents

Rank 1/3

Unstable Currents' Cooldown is reduced to 100 seconds.

Boundless

UpgradeUnstable Currents

Rank 1/3

Lucky Hit: Up to a 25.0% chance to form a Crackling Energy

While Unstable Currents is active, gain the following bonuses:

Increases Crackling Energy damage by 2.5% and reduces Unstable Currents' Cooldown by 0.10 seconds when absorbing Crackling Energy.

Automatically absorb Nearby Crackling Energy.

Damage Bonus

UpgradeFirewall

Rank 1/3

Firewall deals 75%[x] increased damage, but its duration is reduced by 25%[+].
